items.prompt: Which tool helps you look closely at a tiny ant?

options.why: A ruler measures how long something is.
A spoon is for eating. It does not make things look bigger.

hints: The ant is very small.
Which tool makes things look bigger?
Think about what a scientist holds over a tiny bug.
items.explanation: A magnifying glass makes small things look bigger, so we can observe the ant closely.

items.prompt: Does it have wheels? Sort the cards.

figure.alt: Six pictures: a car, a bicycle, a bus, a boat, a kite and a ball.

hints: Look for round parts that turn and roll.
Check each picture for wheels.
Start with the car. How many wheels can you see?
items.explanation: Cars, bicycles and buses have wheels. Boats, kites and balls do not.

items.prompt: Children chose their favourite fruit. How many chose mango?

figure.alt: Tally chart of favourite fruit: mango 7, banana 4, papaya 5.

hints: Find the row for mango.
Each line stands for one child. A gate shape is a group of 5.
Count the group of 5 first, then count on.
items.explanation: The mango row has one group of 5 and 2 more lines. 5 and 2 make 7.

items.prompt: Bayu records the weather for two weeks. How many days were rainy?

figure.title: Weather for two weeks
figure.alt: Pictogram of weather for two weeks: sunny 6 days, rainy 5 days, cloudy 3 days. Each square means 1 day.

hints: Find the row for rainy days.
Each square stands for 1 day.
Point to each square in the rainy row and count.
items.explanation: The rainy row has 5 squares. Each square is 1 day, so 5 days were rainy.

items.prompt: Ayu sorted animals into two groups. What was her rule?

head: Group 1
Group 2
figure.alt: Table of two groups. Group 1: fish, crab, whale. Group 2: cat, camel, lion.

options.why: Group 1 has animals with no legs and a crab with many legs.
Both groups have animals of many colours.

hints: Look for what all the Group 1 animals share.
Think about where each animal lives.
Start with the fish and the whale. Where do they live?
items.explanation: The Group 1 animals live in water. The Group 2 animals live on land. Her rule was where they live.

items.prompt: Match each tool to what it helps you do.
hints: Think about what each tool is used for.
Do the one you have used before first.
Start with the ruler. What do you do with it?
items.explanation: A magnifying glass helps us see small things. A ruler measures length, a thermometer shows how hot something is and a timer measures time.

items.prompt: Sari puts blocks along her desk. How many blocks long is it?

figure.alt: 8 blocks in a line, as long as the desk.

hints: Count each block once.
Touch each block as you count.
Start at one end and count 1, 2, 3.
items.explanation: There are 8 blocks along the desk, so the desk is 8 blocks long.

items.prompt: Tom and Aisha measure the same table with hand spans. Tom counts 6. Aisha counts 8. Why are the numbers different?

figure.alt: Tom measured 6 hand spans. Aisha measured 8 hand spans on the same table.

options.why: It is the same table. Tables do not grow.
Both counts can be right. Aisha needs more spans because her hand is smaller.

hints: The table is the same each time.
Think about what they used to measure.
Compare a big hand and a small hand on the same table.
items.explanation: Aisha's hand span is smaller than Tom's, so she needs more spans to cover the table. A ruler gives the same answer for everyone.

items.prompt: Order the animals from smallest to biggest.

figure.alt: Five animals: a cow, an ant, an elephant, a cat and a mouse.

hints: Start with the tiniest animal.
Picture each animal standing next to you.
Put the ant first, then find the next smallest.
items.explanation: The ant is smallest, then the mouse, the cat and the cow. The elephant is the biggest.

items.prompt: How many more children have a cat than a dog?

figure.title: Our pets
figure.alt: Bar chart of pets: cat 6 children, dog 4 children, fish 3 children, rabbit 2 children.

hints: Find the cat bar and the dog bar.
Read the number at the top of each bar.
The cat bar reaches 6. Now find the top of the dog bar.
items.explanation: 6 children have a cat and 4 have a dog. 6 take away 4 is 2, so 2 more children have a cat.

items.prompt: Which animal can fly and has 6 legs?

figure.alt: Venn diagram with two circles, can fly and has 6 legs. Bird is in can fly only. Bee is where the circles overlap. Ant is in has 6 legs only. Cat is outside both circles.

options.why: A bird can fly, but it has 2 legs.
An ant has 6 legs. Most ants cannot fly.

hints: Look at where the two circles overlap.
The middle part is for animals that match both labels.
Find the word written in the overlap.
items.explanation: A bee can fly and has 6 legs, so it goes in the middle, where the circles overlap.

items.prompt: Mei sorted these things into two groups. What was her rule?

head: Group A
Group B
figure.alt: Table of two groups. Group A: ice cube, snowflake, ice cream. Group B: steam, the Sun, candle flame.

options.why: An ice cube is hard and ice cream is soft, but both are in Group A.
A snowflake is natural and ice cream is made, but both are in Group A.

hints: Look for something every Group A thing shares.
Ask: would you find each one in a freezer or near heat?
Start with the ice cube and the snowflake. What are they like?
items.explanation: Everything in Group A is cold and everything in Group B is hot. Her rule was cold or hot.
